picks.headline: 숨은 변수 몇 개로 거대 물질계를 예측하는 AI
picks.excerpt: National University of Singapore researchers built AI methods that automatically identify a small set of hidden variables capturing a material's collective behavior, letting them predict very large stochastic systems from simulations of much smaller ones. The work (Physical Review Materials and ICML 2026) sharply cuts the compute needed for materials modeling.
picks.rationale: Peer-reviewed method (PRM + ICML 2026) that discovers a few hidden collective variables to predict very large systems from small simulations — directly changes how computational scientists scale materials modeling.

picks.headline: 싱크로트론 실험을 스스로 정렬하는 에이전트형 'X선 과학자'
picks.excerpt: Stanford and SLAC researchers built an agentic AI 'X-ray scientist' that autonomously aligns crystal samples at synchrotron beamlines, reasoning about experimental conditions and issuing instrument commands. Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, it points toward self-running beamline experiments.
picks.rationale: High-credibility (Nature Machine Intelligence), high-novelty result: an agent that reasons about conditions and drives real beamline instruments, a concrete step toward self-running experiments.

picks.headline: 바이오 생산 현장에 맞춘 AI 세포 공학 모델
picks.excerpt: Triplebar Bio, UC Berkeley and BioMADE are developing an AI cell-engineering model built specifically for the biomanufacturing environment to optimize host-cell performance, reduce development timelines and streamline platform design. It targets a data regime that generic protein models miss.
picks.rationale: Applied life-science pick: a purpose-built AI cell-engineering model for the biomanufacturing regime that generic protein models miss — distinct topic and outlet from the earlier Baker protein-design card.

picks.headline: 생명과학 연구에 소리 없이 스며드는 LLM, 경계는 아직 없다
picks.excerpt: A study led by Ivan Jaric warns that LLMs are becoming normalized in life-sciences research before clear usage boundaries exist, potentially eroding cross-disciplinary collaboration and core scientific skills. It argues routine reliance could reshape the foundations of scientific practice and culture.
picks.rationale: A critical, method-level counterpoint on how LLMs are silently reshaping the practice and culture of life-sciences research — balances the tool-launch cards and rounds out topic diversity.
